previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and portal hypertension, was admitted with worsening dyspnea and cough due to a recurrent right pleural effusion. He developed spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, requiring antibiotic treatment, and suffered a variceal bleed that was not amenable to endoscopic banding. He underwent an emergent TIPS procedure, which successfully reduced portal pressure and stopped the bleeding. He received 7 units of packed red blood cells and was managed for hepatic encephalopathy and hyponatremia. A new 2.0 cm liver lesion meeting OPTN 5b criteria was identified on MRI, and cardiac catheterization revealed patent bypass grafts with native coronary disease. The TIPS improved his hydrothorax and ascites, and he was discharged home on medications including ciprofloxacin, lactulose, rifaximin, and reduced-dose warfarin, with plans for transplant evaluation and close follow-up.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of liver, primary, unspecified as to type

PROCEDURE:
1. CT/US-guidedRF ablation of segment 8 hepatic lesion.
2. CT/US-guided RF ablation of segment ___ hepatic lesion.
3. 4.5 L right paracentesis.
PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Following explanation of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The patient
was then brought to the computed tomography suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  General anesthesia was induced by the anesthesiologist. 
Following scout imaging, the skin was marked and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.

Under ultrasound, a cool tip cluster radiofrequency ablation probe (___)
was advanced through the intercostal space until the tip of the probe was just
beyond the expected location of the segment 8 liver lesion.  Radiofrequency
ablation was performed for a total of 12 minutes achieving a temperature of 78
degrees Celsius.  The probe was then repositioned within segment 8 and
radiofrequency ablation was performed for a total of 12 minutes achieving a
temperature 82 degrees Celsius.  The probe was then withdrawn under low energy
to ablate the access tract.

Under ultrasound guidance, ___ needle was advanced into the peritoneal
space until yellow ascites was obtained.  Ultrasound images were saved to PACs
before and after access.  The plastic tubing was slid over the needle, and the
needle was removed.  The tubing was then connected to drainage bottles.  A
total of 4.5 L of yellow ascites was removed.

Under ultrasound, a cool tip cluster radiofrequency ablation probe (___)
was advanced through the intercostal space until the tip of the probe was just
beyond the expected location of the segment ___ liver lesion.  Appropriate
positioning was confirmed with a noncontrast CT.  Radiofrequency ablation was
performed for a total of 12 minutes achieving a temperature of 75 degrees
Celsius.  The probe was then withdrawn under low energy to ablate the access
tract.

Contrast enhanced multiphase computed tomography was obtained.  The skin was
then cleaned and dry sterile dressings were applied. The patient was awakened
from general anesthesia without incident and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications. The patient was transferred to the
post-anesthesia care unit for further monitoring.

FINDINGS: 

Hypoechoic lesion in hepatic segment 8 targeted with ultrasound and CT
guidance.  Post ablation imaging demonstrates appropriate ablation zone in the
region of this lesion.
Hypoechoic lesion in hepatic segment ___ targeted with ultrasound and CT
guidance.  Post ablation imaging demonstrates appropriate ablation zone in the
region of the lesion.

The liver is nodular in contour, compatible with known cirrhosis.  Prior

Gallstones are noted within the gallbladder.  Moderate ascites is noted.
